query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the outcome/magnitude of delay itself, not a constitutive aspect OF the reasons for delay. It measures how long, not which facet of causation. It restates the phenomenon rather than decomposing its reasons.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is an attribute of the incident that may correlate with or predict delay, but it is an external driver, not a part-of the concept 'delay reasons'. It is not an aspect of the reason itself.

per_column.name: category_criticality
per_column.rationale: Criticality of the category is a covariate that may explain variation in delay, but it is an external predictor rather than a constitutive facet of the reasons for delay.

per_column.name: is_weekend_opened
per_column.rationale: Whether opened on a weekend is a potential causal/contextual factor of delay, not an aspect that is part-of the delay-reasons concept. It is a candidate cause, not a facet.

judge.rationale: A faceted decomposition of 'incident_delay_reasons' would require columns that are constitutive parts/aspects of the reasons for delay itself -- e.g., wait-for-vendor time, awaiting-customer time, reassignment/bouncing, diagnostic/investigation time, approval/change-management delay, resource-availability contention. None of the added columns are meronymic parts of the reason concept. resolution_time_hours restates the delay outcome; priority_level and category_criticality are external predictors; is_weekend_opened is a candidate cause/context. Because no columns qualify as facets, both mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness are 0.
